title: Train Fault Library Standard Schema
description: JSON Schema for the Train Fault Library Standard (TFLS)

meta.description: Metadata about the train type and operator

name.description: Full name of the train type/model

code.description: Short code identifying the train type

yearIntroduced.description: Year when this train type was introduced to service

schemaVersion.description: Version of the TFRS schema being used

lastUpdated.description: Date when this fault reference was last updated

maintainer.description: Email contact for maintenance of this reference file

additionalNotes.description: Any additional notes about this reference file

categorySource.description: Optional statement of where the faults' category values come from: manual when they are the operator's own classification as written in its manuals, editorial when the library's author chose them. Applications show categories as a severity only when this is manual

manuals.description: Optional list of manuals that faults can reference. Manual PDFs are distributed alongside the .tfls file in a TFLS package (.tflsx)

id.description: Identifier for this manual, unique within the file. Faults reference manuals by this id

documentNumber.description: Optional document or part number of the manual, written the way other manuals cite it (e.g. TAN 152). Applications may link mentions of it in other manuals

revision.description: Optional revision or edition of the manual

effectiveDate.description: Optional date from which this revision of the manual applies

group.description: Optional volume, chapter or system the manual belongs to (e.g. Volume 6 – Faults and failures, or Brakes). Applications group manuals by it when browsing

file.description: Optional path of the manual's PDF inside the TFLS package, relative to the .tfls file and using forward slashes (e.g. manuals/drivers-manual.pdf)

faults.description: List of all potential faults for this train type

id.description: Optional identifier for this entry, unique within the file and kept the same from one version of the file to the next. Applications use it to remember bookmarked and recently viewed faults

faultCode.description: Optional identifier for the fault within this operator's systems

system.description: The train system to which this fault belongs

category.description: Optional severity or importance classification of the fault. Leave it out rather than guessing; applications hide the classification when it is absent

description.description: Optional detailed description of the fault

symptoms.description: Optional observable symptoms of this fault

rectificationSteps.description: Optional steps to rectify the fault

procedure.description: Optional structured form of rectificationSteps, saying who performs each step and in which situation. Applications use it in place of rectificationSteps when present; keep rectificationSteps as well so older applications still show the steps

text.description: What to do, without the actor or context written in front of it

actor.description: Optional role that performs the step, as the manual names it (e.g. Driver, Guard, Train Crew)

context.description: Optional situation the step applies to, as the manual names it (e.g. In service, Out depot). Steps of a fault that share a context are alternatives to the steps of its other contexts, not a continuation of them

notes.description: Optional additional notes, warnings, or special instructions

manualReferences.description: Optional references to the pages of manuals that cover this fault

manual.description: The id of a manual listed in meta.manuals

page.description: Optional page of the PDF to open, counting the first page of the file as 1 (not the printed page number)

section.description: Optional section number or heading in the manual (e.g. 4.2 Brake Cylinder Faults). Without a page, applications may open the manual at the bookmark or heading with this title
